text.p: Tele-Communications Inc said Thursday that it has signed a 15-year agreement to carry the C-SPAN public affairs cable network.
"This should erase once and for all any doubts about the future of this great network, or about TCI's commitment to it," said TCI President Leo Hindery, who announced the agreement here.

Hindery said that 100 percent of TCI's customers would have access to both of C-SPAN's channels within three years. About 97 percent of its customers now have access to C-SPAN I, while about two-thirds have access to C-SPAN II.

Hindery, who recently joined the Englewood, Colo.-based company, also said TCI would join forces with Court TV to launch a multi-million dollar five-year public affairs program in its cable systems around the country.
"Court TV's local forums and creative presentations will focus on exposing young people in the communities we serve to the evil consequences of violence in our society," he said.
